title: Reading and Building Graphs
subject: Maths
learning_objectives: Read a pictograph using its key
Build a bar chart from data

sections.title: Graphs tell stories with pictures
sections.content: A graph shows numbers as a picture, so you can compare things at a glance. Today we will read a pictograph, read a bar chart, and even build one ourselves!

sections.title: Muffins sold at the bake sale

sections.question: Each 🧁 symbol means 2 muffins. How many chocolate muffins were sold?
sections.hint: Count the chocolate symbols, then multiply by 2 — check the key!
sections.correct_feedback: Yes! 4 symbols × 2 muffins each = 8 chocolate muffins.
sections.incorrect_feedback: Careful — each symbol stands for 2 muffins, not 1. Chocolate has 4 symbols, so 4 × 2 = 8.

sections.statement: More children have dogs than cats.
sections.hint: Compare the heights of the Dogs bar and the Cats bar.
sections.correct_feedback: Right! The Dogs bar (7) is taller than the Cats bar (5).
sections.incorrect_feedback: Look again: the Dogs bar reaches 7 and the Cats bar reaches 5, so dogs win.

sections.instruction: The fruit stall sold 6 apples, 4 bananas, and 8 oranges. Drag each bar to the right height!
sections.hint: Read each number in the story and slide that bar up until it matches.
sections.correct_feedback: Perfect graph! You showed 6 apples, 4 bananas, and 8 oranges.
sections.incorrect_feedback: Check each bar against the story: apples 6, bananas 4, oranges 8.

completion_message: Amazing! You can read pictographs, read bar charts, and even build your own graph!
